prompt: Estimate the number of ATMs in Delhi.

clarifications.answer: You are estimating physical ATM machines, not cards.
Count all ATMs regardless of who operates them.
Take Delhi's population as about 3 crore.

common_traps: Estimating ATM cards and forgetting to convert cards into machines via a cards-per-ATM ratio.
Using one flat cards-per-ATM ratio instead of splitting by area density.
Multiplying by population instead of households, double-counting people in the same home.

anchors.1: No chain from people to machines; guesses a number, or estimates ATM cards and stops without converting cards into machines.
anchors.3: Builds a household-to-cards chain but never states the cards-per-ATM ratio, or applies it vaguely.
anchors.5: Chooses a household-to-cards-to-machines chain and states the cards-per-ATM assumption explicitly.

anchors.1: Applies one flat ratio to the whole city with no segmentation.
anchors.3: Segments, but with an arbitrary split not tied to a real driver of ATM density.
anchors.5: Splits by area density (or an equivalent), rather than one blanket ratio.

anchors.1: Botches crore/lakh conversions or lands far outside any plausible range.
anchors.3: Reaches an answer but with a conversion slip, or lands just outside the 3000-6000 range.
anchors.5: Carries crore/lakh conversions cleanly and lands in the 3000-6000 range.

anchors.1: No sanity check; states the number as final.
anchors.3: Mentions a check but doesn't carry it through, or the check doesn't actually test the estimate.
anchors.5: Validates via ATM throughput, e.g. transactions per ATM per day implying each card is used at least monthly.
